points.description: States that a single-layer perceptron cannot solve (or cannot solve effectively) the XOR problem because XOR is not linearly separable / the perceptron can only learn linear decision boundaries.
points.partial_credit: Half if it says the perceptron fails on XOR but gives no reason (no mention of linear separability/linear features).

points.description: States that a multilayer perceptron can solve XOR because it can learn non-linear features / non-linear decision boundaries (e.g. via hidden layers and non-linear activations).
points.partial_credit: Half if it says the MLP can solve XOR but gives no reason (no mention of non-linearity or hidden layers).

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) need both: perceptron fails on XOR due to linear-only/linear separability limits, and MLP succeeds due to non-linear features. Give 1 mark total if only one side is correct or both sides are stated without reasons. Give 0 for reversed or unrelated answers. Clear synonyms (e.g. 'straight line boundary', 'hidden layers') are accepted.
